{{nihongo|'''Unebiyamaguchi Shrine'''|畝火山口神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Unebiyamaguchi Shrine''' (うねびやまぐちじんじゃ, おむねやまじんじゃ<ref name="a">On the signboard in front of the Mt. Unebi trailhead by the shrine, “畝火山口” is given the reading “おむねやま”.</ref>) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} on the western foot of {{ill|Mount Unebi|Q17606448|qid=Q17606448}} in {{ill|Kashihara, Nara|Q496319|qid=Q496319}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is popularly called “Omine-yama.” It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was prefectural shrine.

It is one of the six Yamaguchi shrines in Yamato listed in the norito of the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} ({{ill|Asuka-ni-Imasu Shrine|Q11665959|qid=Q11665959|lt=Asuka}}, Ishimura, Osa, Hase, '''Unebi''', and {{ill|Miminashi Yamaguchi Shrine|Q11610732|qid=Q11610732|lt=Miminashi}}), and one of the 85 shrines of the rain-prayer rites in the {{ill|special festivals|Q11612499|qid=Q11612499}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
It enshrines Okinagatarashihime-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}), {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Q2983724|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke-hime-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013|lt=Uwatsutsuo-no-Mikoto}}. Based on the tradition that Empress Jingū gave birth to Emperor Ōjin, it is worshiped as a deity of safe childbirth.

From examples of other {{ill|Yamaguchi shrines|Q11467399|qid=Q11467399}} and the shrine’s character, the original deity is thought to have been {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Ōyamatsumi|Q386563|qid=Q386563|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi-no-Mikoto}}. Today Ōyamatsumi-no-Mikoto is enshrined in the auxiliary Ōyamatsumi Shrine.

=== History ===
The origin of the foundation is unknown. The first documentary appearance is in ''Shinshō Kakuchokufu-shō'', which records one shrine household granted in {{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}} ({{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191}} 1). In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} it appears as “Unebi Yamaguchi-za Shrine, Takachi District, Yamato Province,” is listed as a great shrine, and is recorded as receiving offerings at monthly and Niiname rites.

Originally it stood on the western foot of Mt. Unebi. In the ''Gogun Jinjaki'' of {{ill|Bun'an|fa|بون‌آن|fr|Ère Bunnan|ia|Bunnan|ja|文安|ko|분안|ru|Бунъан|simple|Bun'an|sr|Бунан|sv|Bunnan|tr|Bun'an|zh|文安 (日本)|qid=Q1193586}} 3 ({{ill|1446|ab|1446|af|1446|als|1446|am|1446 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1446|ar|1446|ary|1446|arz|1446|ast|1446|avk|1446|az|1446|azb|۱۴۴۶ (میلادی)|be|1446|be_x_old|1446|bg|1446|bjn|1446|bn|১৪৪৬|bpy|মারি ১৪৪৬|br|1446|bs|1446.|ca|1446|cdo|1446 nièng|ceb|1446|ckb|١٤٤٦|crh|1446|cs|1446|csb|1446|cv|1446|cy|1446|da|1446|de|1446|diq|1446|el|1446|eml|1446|eo|1446|es|1446|et|1446|eu|1446|fa|۱۴۴۶ (میلادی)|fi|1446|fo|1446|fr|1446|frr|1446|fy|1446|ga|1446|gan|1446年|gcr|1446|gd|1446|gl|1446|he|1446|hi|१४४६|hr|1446.|ht|1446 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1446|hy|1446|ia|1446|id|1446|ilo|1446|io|1446|is|1446|it|1446|ja|1446年|jv|1446|ka|1446|kaa|1446|kk|1446 жыл|ko|1446년|la|1446|lb|1446|li|1446|lij|1446|lmo|1446|lt|1446 m.|lv|1446. gads|mai|१४४६|map_bms|1446|mdf|1446|mhr|1446|mi|1446|min|1446|mk|1446|mr|इ.स. १४४६|mrj|1446 и|ms|1446|my|၁၄၄၆|mzn|۱۴۴۶|nah|1446|nap|1446|nds|1446|new|सन् १४४६|nl|1446|nn|1446|no|1446|nrm|1446|nso|1446|oc|1446|or|୧୪୪୬|os|1446-æм аз|pl|1446|pnb|1446|pt|1446|qu|1446|ro|1446|ru|1446 год|rue|1446|sa|१४४६|sah|1446|sc|1446|scn|1446|sd|1446ع|se|1446|sh|1446.|shn|1446|si|1446|simple|1446|sk|1446|sl|1446|smn|1446|sq|1446|sr|1446|su|1446|sv|1446|sw|1446|ta|1446|tg|Соли 1446|th|พ.ศ. 1989|tk|1446|tl|1446|tly|1446|tr|1446|tt|1446 ел|uk|1446|ur|1446ء|uz|1446|vec|1446|vi|1446|vls|1446|wa|1446|war|1446|wuu|1446年|xmf|1446|zh|1446年|zh_min_nan|1446 nî|zh_yue|1446年|qid=Q6430}}), it is described as “at Kume-gō, western mountain tail of Mt. Unebi.” But maps of the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} era place it on the summit, meaning it was moved from the foot to the summit between Bun'an and Tenshō. The shrine name evolved from Unebi-za Yamaguchi Shrine; in the Edo period it was also called “Unebi Myōjin” and “Unebi-yama Jingū-sha.”

In {{ill|1940|Q18633|qid=Q18633}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ka|შოვას პერიოდი|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}} 15), when major expansion works were carried out at {{ill|Kashihara Shrine|arz|ضريح كاشيهارا|de|Kashihara-jingū|es|Santuario de Kashihara|fa|معبد کاشی‌هارا|fr|Kashihara-jingū|ja|橿原神宮|ko|가시하라 신궁|la|Templum Cashihara|zh|橿原神宮|qid=Q710333}} on the eastern foot of Mt. Unebi, it was deemed, in the climate of the high tide of {{ill|Kōkoku shikan|fr|Vision historique du Japon impérial|ja|皇国史観|ko|황국사관|zh|皇国史观|zh_min_nan|Hông-kok sú-koan|qid=Q5368837}}, that looking down over Kashihara Jingū and Emperor Jinmu’s mausoleum would “defile divine authority”<ref>According to the explanatory notice at the torii of Unebiyamaguchi Shrine.</ref>. The Japanese government therefore ordered relocation to the western foot (current site). At that time it was promoted from {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} to prefectural shrine.

=== Rituals ===
A special ritual called “Hani-tsuchi ritual” is held. It takes soil from the summit of Mt. Unebi for making earthenware used at {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}} in the {{ill|Kinensai|Q118906710|qid=Q118906710}} (February) and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}} (November). On that occasion, those performing the rite customarily prepare their ritual garments at {{ill|Kawamata Shrine (Q11553360)|Q11553360|qid=Q11553360}} before heading to this shrine.

* December 3: New grain thanksgiving festival
* 1st of every month: {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161}}, 15th: Birth report festival
